body.estimand_functional: \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI}}=I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}\) when \(s=1\); when \(1<s\le2\), \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI}}\) is the connected hull from the bias-aware transformed-outcome test centered at \(\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}\), with the explicit \(MR_c\) location-bias term retained.

sampling_model.design: Independent random design with \(X_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and a law-specific unknown cutoff \(c_P\in[1/4,3/4]\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument is \(Z_i=\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge c_P\}\), and monotone response types imply \(D_i=D_i(Z_i)\).
sampling_model.outcome: Binary potential outcomes obey consistency \(Y_i=Y_i(D_i)\); exclusion is encoded by the absence of a direct \(Z_i\) argument.
sampling_model.overlap: Uniformly on both sides of the cutoff, \(\operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid X=x,\ell)\ge v\) and the absolute conditional outcome--treatment correlation is at most \(1-v\); when the conditional treatment variance is zero, covariance is zero and the correlation inequality is interpreted directly without forming a correlation coefficient.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: One-sided observable treatment and outcome regressions admit radius-\(M\), order-\(s\) H\"older extensions, with no equality imposed on their derivatives at the cutoff. The proved \(s=1\) interval uses deterministic four-fold rectangular scanning and fixed-center inversion. For \(s>1\), the proved cutoff component residualizes a candidate jump against a continuous broken line, fits separate degree-one flank regressions, and refines by cross-fold residual-loss classification.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Theorem 1 gives honest bias-aware Anderson--Rubin inference when the cutoff is known.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The Lipschitz strong-signal theorem proves unknown-cutoff oracle-order connected length; the higher-smoothness extension remains the detectable-region open question.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Theorem 4 gives \(n\)-consistent cutoff estimation under a fixed discontinuity.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The Lipschitz strong-signal theorem allows \(\kappa_n\to0\) and proves uniform honest connected-interval length.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their ordered-modulus construction controls expected length on convex fixed-index regression classes.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present unknown-location causal ratio problem is a nonconvex translated union; the exact critical expression remains open.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Proposition 4.2 gives a matched cutoff-location rate under a derivative jump bounded away from zero.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The profile-localization lemma treats a vanishing level jump and profiles an unrestricted derivative kink, but the full \(s>1\) interval frontier remains open.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their multiscale procedure gives change-point inference for step functions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: It informs the coarse scan architecture but does not supply the causal weak-LATE connected-length theorem.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: They provide general maximal control for empirical-process suprema.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Their tools inform concentration architecture; the displayed sequential exponential localization is derived here for the profiled cutoff criterion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: They study aligned multivariate nonparametric change-point detection and localization.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Their model does not impose the monotone fuzzy-RD causal coupling or target fixed-level connected LATE length.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Bayesian model propagates posterior uncertainty about an unknown fuzzy-RD cutoff.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present result is frequentist and minimax; only its \(s=1\) oracle-order face is proved.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their working paper treats fuzzy RD and unknown-discontinuity estimation in separate high-dimensional extensions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: It does not determine the joint vanishing-jump, unknown-cutoff connected-length frontier studied here.

body.tldr: The paper studies fixed-\(\alpha\) expected length of connected honest intervals for fuzzy-RD LATE when the compliance jump and its unknown cutoff weaken jointly. The location-mixture construction proves a finite-sample nonshrinking converse below the signal-to-entropy boundary. At \(s=1\), an explicit four-fold scan--refine--invert map attains the known-cutoff order once \(n\kappa_n^3\) dominates \(\log(e/\kappa_n)\). For \(s>1\), a new degree-one profile criterion localizes the cutoff without derivative matching, but the same-class interval frontier remains the explicit bracket question \(L_n\asymp\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n+1/(n\kappa_n^3)\}\).

project_justification.gap: Known-cutoff weak fuzzy-RD inference and fixed-jump unknown-cutoff localization do not characterize honest connected LATE-interval length when both the compliance denominator and its location weaken. In particular, neither result controls the transformed-outcome effect of an unrestricted cross-cutoff slope kink.
project_justification.niche: The joint experiment combines a nonconvex location union, a causal outcome--treatment ratio, and fixed-level connected-length loss. The Lipschitz face has an attainable oracle reduction, while for \(s>1\) cutoff localization and post-localization slope-kink bias are distinct statistical components.
project_justification.fill: The project gives one observable reduced-form class, embeds outcome-invariant monotone location mixtures to prove the finite-sample converse, supplies a fully explicit oracle-order four-fold interval at \(s=1\), and proves a slope-profiled \(s>1\) cutoff estimator with exponential localization. The remaining higher-smoothness contribution is honestly posed as the bracket with terms \(\rho_n/\kappa_n\) and \(1/(n\kappa_n^3)\), including a matching slope-kink converse.

body.related_work: Noack and Rothe (2024) supply the known-cutoff bias-aware Anderson--Rubin benchmark, but not unknown-cutoff connected expected length. Porter and Yu (2015) prove fixed-jump cutoff localization in a sharp-design model; the theorem here instead permits \(\kappa_n\to0\) and proves oracle-order honest length at \(s=1\). Frick, Munk, and Sieling (2014) and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014) inform scan and maximal-control architecture, but neither gives this causal localization-to-length result. M{\"u}ller and Song (1997) and Tuvaandorj (2020) study location experiments rather than weak-denominator LATE intervals. Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018) treat convex fixed-index classes. Madrid Padilla, Yu, Wang, and Rinaldo (2022) study aligned multivariate change channels without the monotone fuzzy-RD causal constraints. Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version) use Bayesian unknown-cutoff inference, and Arai, Otsu, and Seo (2026) treat fuzzy and unknown-discontinuity extensions separately. The proved results here are the finite-sample location-mixture converse, the \(s=1\) oracle-attainment theorem, and slope-robust profile localization for \(s>1\); the full higher-smoothness interval bracket is not claimed as determined or sharp.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Oracle-order strong-signal interval length is proved only at \(s=1\). For \(1<s\le2\), the cutoff itself is now localized by a proved slope-profiled criterion with tail \(\exp(-c n\kappa_n^2u)\), but the complete fourth-fold honesty and expected-length calculation with the \(MR_c\) term, and the matching in-class slope-kink lower pairs, remain open. The exact fixed-\(\alpha\) critical-window law also remains open.
body.honest_scope: The Wald interpretation, the known-cutoff benchmark, and the finite-sample outcome-invariant location-mixture converse retain their full stated scope. The explicit oracle-attainment result is uniform only on the Lipschitz face \(s=1\). For \(s>1\), only slope-robust cutoff localization is proved; the bracket \(\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n+1/(n\kappa_n^3)\}\) and its oracle subface \(n\kappa_n^2\rho_n\gtrsim1\) are questions, not conclusions. No cross-side derivative compatibility, latent-cell smoothness, adaptation, disconnected-set, or Bayesian-calibration claim is added.
body.interpretation: At \(s=1\), the information \(n\kappa_n^3\) pays the logarithmic search cost and the independent fourth-fold inversion then has the same \(n^{-1/3}/\kappa_n\) length as if the cutoff were known. For \(s>1\), profiling a candidate step against \(1,u,(u-q)_+\) removes the side-slope mismatch from cutoff localization and yields error \(R_c\asymp(n\kappa_n^2)^{-1}\). The unchanged class nevertheless lets a transformed-outcome derivative kink turn that location error into LATE error of order \(MR_c/\kappa_n\asymp1/(n\kappa_n^3)\).
